label: lr-72c47
summary: The model's churn score rests mainly on two effects. Customer-service calls: the predicted risk is flat up to two calls and climbs steeply from three (typical customer: 1.1% at two calls, 9.9% at four, 66.7% at six). Heavy daytime use without a voice-mail plan switches on a heavy-use detector that raises the risk sharply (0.9% at 200 day minutes, above 99% at 300 day minutes without a voice-mail plan, 0.4% with one) and also moves the calls threshold up; below that hinge more daytime use lowers the risk slightly. An international plan adds a direct term (typical risk 1.1% without, 15.5% with), fewer international calls raise the risk, and per-state offsets, a tenure hinge and small evening, night and area-code terms add the rest. Switching off the usage-and-calls part lowers the training AUC from 0.920 to 0.658.

tool_bugs: (1) probe_concept's expression evaluator refuses .clip() on a compound expression (AttributeError: 'BinOp' object has no attribute 'value'); worked around with (x > a) * (x - a). (2) Not a bug but a constraint that shaped the hierarchy: an exit of one leaf cannot be an entry of another leaf ('already covered'), and unit 469 feeds both the heavy-use readout and the calls gate, so heavy use and calls had to share one deep leaf. (3) add_identity_node must leave one input at the target, so the tiny area-code-415 direct edge stays in the root. (4) probe_concept scores a multi-exit leaf by the mean over exits, so the two sums of the usage leaf were merged into one identity exit (idUseCs) before probing.

overall_function: The network adds a handful of terms on the score scale and passes the sum through a sigmoid. The main term is a hinge in customer-service calls: flat for few calls, then rising steeply. A second hinge switches on for heavy daytime (and evening) use without a voice-mail plan and raises the score sharply; below that hinge more daytime use lowers it slightly, and heavy use also moves the calls threshold up, the one interaction in the model. An international plan raises the score directly and more international calls lower it, longer tenure raises it slightly past a threshold, heavier evening use lowers it slightly through a separate hinge, and fitted per-state offsets (Hawaii and Vermont down, California and Washington up) shift it by state; area code barely matters. Most state indicators, the voice-mail message count, evening calls and the night and international charges have no edge and are ignored.
clinical_terms: In customer terms: the model predicts that a customer will leave mainly when they have made many customer-service calls (risk climbs steeply past a few calls) or are heavy daytime users without a voice-mail plan, whose risk jumps sharply once day use passes a high level; for heavy users it takes more service calls before the calls add further risk. Having an international plan raises the predicted risk, especially with few international calls; long-standing accounts are slightly riskier, heavier evening use slightly less risky, and a few states carry their own fitted offsets.
stuck: Hierarchy constraint: unit 469 feeds both the heavy-use readout and the calls gate, and an exit of one leaf cannot be the entry of another, so heavy use and calls share one deep leaf whose concept probe is partial. probe_concept averages exits, so its two sums were merged into one identity exit. The per-state direct offsets have no concept reading (closed form only). No time pressure: finished well inside the box.
